signalslinkep:usageinfo-signalslinkep-ti: SignalsLink.EP - Integration between the Signals and Electrical Progressive mods
signalslinkep:usageinfo-signalslinkep-te:
SignalsLink.EP
Extends the Signals mod with components that work with the Electrical Progressive mod.

If you want to switch an electrical circuit on and off with a signal, use the EP switch. It is useful wherever a machine should run only when there is a reason for it.
If you need to know the state of the electrical grid, use the EP meter. Depending on the signal at its input, it reports battery charge, the production and consumption balance, or cable load, allowing you to start backup power sources or disconnect consumers before the cable burns out.
signalslinkep:block-handbooktext-epmeter:
Allows obtaining information about the state of the electrical grid to which the meter is connected. What it measures is determined by the signal at the input.
What the meter reports
Input 1 — battery charge. The output signal shows the charge level of the batteries in the grid. 0 - batteries are empty, 15 - batteries are fully charged.
Input 2 — production and consumption balance. Values 1-7: more is consumed than produced, 8: consumption=production, 9-15: electricity production exceeds consumption.
Input 3 — current in the cable. The output signal shows the current flow in the cables of the block to which the meter is connected. Values 0-12 represent current from 0 to the maximum cable capacity. 13-15 represent cable overload (it is probably already smoldering and will soon burn out).
Other signal — the output signal is 0.
signalslinkep:block-handbooktext-epswitc:
A signal-controlled switch. Allows switching electrical current transmission on or off.
Connectors
Input — if there is a signal on it, the switch is on. If there is no signal on it, the switch is off.
